subject: [RFC] Robust futex causing memcg OOM storm on exit

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed Michal Hocko's concern about the effectiveness of MMF_OOM_SKIP, provided test results showing that adding tsk_is_oom_victim check improves performance, and suggested proceeding with the early nomem change, but acknowledged a desire to deploy in prod sooner.
reviews.raw_body:
Here are the results with the reproducer I have. Ran the test 5 times and
showing avg and std below:

Baseline (next-20260726)			36.47  0.78 s
early nomem (tsk_is_oom_victim + MMF_OOM_SKIP)	20.83  4.19 s
early nomem (tsk_is_oom_victim)			 0.59  0.22 s

Since MMF_OOM_SKIP is set after multiple retries by the oom_reaper the result in
between baseline and simple tsk_is_oom_victim check makes sense.

I think we can proceed with the early nomem (tsk_is_oom_victim + MMF_OOM_SKIP)
change as it is more conservative unless you have concerns. Overall I want to
deploy this in prod sooner to see if this specific issues is resolved or we
catch something else.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt (author)
reviews.summary: Author addressed a concern about inconsistent results on virtual machines, reported improved and consistent results on a physical machine, and confirmed they will send a revised patch.
reviews.raw_body:
Now I have much better results. Previous numbers were on a VM and now I have
ran on a physical machine and the results are much better and consistent. The
baseline consistently shows ~90 seconds exit time while (tsk_is_oom_victim +
MMF_OOM_SKIP) consistently show ~3 seconds exit time. I will send the formal
patch soon.

2026-07-28.patch_summary: This patch addresses a memory cgroup (memcg) Out-Of-Memory (OOM) issue caused by robust futexes on exit. The problem occurs when the kernel tries to reap queued tasks, leading to an OOM storm. To fix this, the patch adds a check for MMF_OOM_REAP_QUEUED in the mm_flags_test function.
